title: api: standardize rate-limit semantics, idempotency for streaming + OpenAI compat
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Streaming endpoints and the OpenAI-compat layer had inconsistent rate-limit and idempotency behavior across code paths. Customers saw two classes of issues: 1) clients receiving 429s without a Retry-After header or with conflicting Retry-After semantics (seconds vs RFC-1123 date), and 2) duplicate function/tool calls when streaming reconnects occurred and idempotency keys were not propagated or honored for chunked/streamed responses. Motivation: standardize server behavior to match the documented OpenAI-compatible API surface while keeping Redwood-specific headers for observability.

Summary of changes: consolidated rate-limit handling into a single middleware so all API surfaces (text generation, streaming, function/tool-calls, embeddings) return consistent 429 semantics (Retry-After as seconds when within 1 day, RFC-1123 otherwise) and include a new normalized header X-Redwood-RetryAfter-Seconds for downstream tooling. Idempotency: extended idempotency-first semantics to streaming by lifting idempotency-key validation into the request ingress and persisting idempotency metadata for the lifetime of a stream (KV-backed, TTL 24h). On reconnects, the server will reconcile partial responses and avoid re-executing tools if a matching idempotency key exists.

Compatibility notes: default behavior preserves existing SDK compatibility. OpenAI-compat layer now returns consistent error bodies (type, message, code) for 429 and 5xx errors so clients implementing OpenAI semantics see predictable payloads. We intentionally do not change 200 response shapes.

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate rate-limit handling middleware and unify Retry-After output format
- [x] Persist idempotency metadata for streaming sessions and tool calls
- [x] Add reconciliation logic to avoid duplicate tool/function invocations on stream reconnect
- [x] Add unit/integration tests for Retry-After header variants and idempotency reconnection scenarios
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat docs and SDK tests
- [x] Canary rollout plan and feature flag for idempotency storage TTL tuning

Testing & validation: added unit tests for the middleware and end-to-end integration tests using perf-canary that simulate 100k streaming tokens across 2000 connections with induced mid-stream disconnects. Canary observed 0 duplicated tool invocations after reconciliation logic was added (down from baseline ~3.7%). CI: expanded test matrix to run openai-compat integration suite.

Rollout plan: staged canary across production edge nodes under feature-flag 'streaming-idempotency-v2' for 48 hours, monitor metrics: duplicated_tool_invocations, stream_reconnect_rate, rate_limit_429_count, retry_after_missing. After two successful canaries and green health checks we will enable by default and backfill the idempotency cache for ongoing streams for affected customers using a controlled migration tool.

Notes: this touches rate-limiter internals and idempotency storage; ops were engaged and a rollback playbook is in the PR description. See linked Linear ENG-8421 for performance tuning follow-ups.

review_comments: Aarav Patel (2026-02-21): Nice consolidation. Request: add a unit test for the RFC-1123 path when Retry-After > 86400 seconds. Also prefer seconds-based header for internal tooling; can we expose X-Redwood-RetryAfter-Seconds?
Maya Chen (2026-02-21): Added X-Redwood-RetryAfter-Seconds and unit test for RFC-1123 path. See tests/unit/test_rate_limiter.py:TestRetryAfter::test_rfc1123
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-23): Concern: idempotency TTL 24h may be high for some customers. Suggest making TTL configurable per-customer and default to 6h. Can we add a feature-flagged config?
Maya Chen (2026-02-23): Agreed. Added feature flag 'streaming-idempotency-v2' and per-tenant override. Default kept at 24h during canary; plan to reduce to 6h after tuning (ENG-8421 follow-up).
Lucas Ortega (2026-02-25): Integration tests look good. One nit: ensure error body includes 'type' and 'code' fields for downstream SDKs that switch on error.code. Updated errors.py accordingly.
Maya Chen (2026-02-25): Fixed. Error payloads now follow schema: { type: string, message: string, code: string }.
CI (2026-02-26): flaky test test_stream_reconnects timed out on first run; re-run passed after increasing timeout. Recorded in CI job 5421 for future flakiness tracking.
release_notes:
- Standardize 429/Retry-After semantics across API surfaces (OpenAI-compat and Redwood native)
- Add X-Redwood-RetryAfter-Seconds header for tooling
- Persist idempotency metadata for streaming sessions to prevent duplicate tool/function invocations on reconnects
- OpenAI-compat: consistent error payloads for 429 and 5xx (type, message, code)
- Canary rollout behind feature flag 'streaming-idempotency-v2'
backout_plan: If canary shows increased duplication or latency regressions (>5% increase in p95 token latency or >0.5% duplicated_tool_invocations), flip feature flag off and run controlled backfill rollback script to clear in-flight idempotency keys. Ops runbook: revert middleware change and re-enable previous rate-limiter behavior.
notes: Ops and Security reviewed storage design for idempotency metadata (KV with encryption-at-rest). No PII stored; only request hashes and tool invocation fingerprints. Performance impact observed <3% tail latency increase during local load tests; we tuned kernel batching to compensate (see ENG-8421).
